Off the mark at the Curragh in March on first outing for current trainer and not disgraced when fifth of 15 at Listowel (1½m, good to soft) last week, having every chance back at a more suitable trip after a further 2 mo

Very lightly-raced 6-y-o who got off the mark in maiden at Roscommon in July 2024. Low-key reappearance at the Curragh in March and was never involved having been off a further 5 months off at former course 4 weeks ago.

Sole career success for Charlie Johnston came over 1¾m at Redcar in 2024 and in good order over hurdles last season, scoring at Naas back in December. Below form in a couple of starts in the spring and returns to the lev
Added to an increasingly unappealing profile since his juvenile hurdling days when tailed off at Listowel 4 days ago. Back on the level but easy enough to look elsewhere.

Better on all-weather than turf but wasn't seen to best effect the way things panned out when seventh of 14 at Dundalk (10.5f) just over 6 weeks ago. Back up in trip and worth a second look from his much-reduced mark.

Stepped up on reappearance run to open his account on the level in 7-runner handicap at Tramore (1½m, good to soft) just over 6 weeks ago, getting first run. By no means handicapped out of things from 4 lb higher so bold

Made winning start for Richard Hughes over at Brighton in June and improved with each start since, notching a third success at Newbury (1½m, good to firm) in July. Failed to meet market expectations at former course earl

Confirmed previous form when winning 13-runner handicap at Gowran in May. Clearly wasn't 100% on the day upped in grade at Ballinrobe (13f, good to soft) the following month and hasn't been seen since. First-time tongue

Won twice for current yard last season and arrives in top form, proving himself at this trip back from a break when fourth of 15 in handicap at Roscommon (1½m, good to soft) 4 weeks ago. High on the shortlist.

Built on debut promise with cosy win in 7-runner course maiden in July. Improved again when fifth on handicap debut at the Curragh and shaped much better than the result when ninth of 15 at Roscommon (1½m) 4 weeks ago, f

Won at this meeting last year and proved better than ever when notching his third career success at Galway in July. Shaped better than the distance beaten suggested when seventh of 15 at Galway (1½m, soft) just under 3 w
Mid-field in 3 maidens so far but could show more now handicapping in first-time cheekpieces.

Left hurdling debut form behind with an effort much more in keeping with the level he reached on the Flat when second of 9 in juvenile hurdle at this course (17f, good) last month (tongue tied). One to look out for back
Yet to score this term and seemed unsuited by the return to 1m when eighth of 14 at Punchestown recently. Back up in trip. RESERVE.

Opened his account under a change of tactics when making all at Leopardstown in July. Backed that up at the second attempt when good second there last month and added another placed effort to his tally at Listowel last w
Won at Dundalk in February and has been shaping up well in turf handicaps, again running well when second of 14 at Punchestown (9f, good) recently. Significantly back up in trip. RESERVE.

races.name: Follow AtTheRaces On Instagram EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
races.verdict: MAJESTIC FLAME had a possible excuse last time and is given a second chance to confirm her debut promise. Last-time-out C&D second Speed Nation is the obvious danger on form. Ambience is worth a look in the betting back from a breathing operation.

runners.note: 11/4 and tongue tied, sixth of 7 in novice at Newmarket (6f, good to firm) on debut in May. Not seen since (has had breathing operation) but seemingly thought capable of better based on her prominence in the betting at N
Down the field on all 3 starts and won't be of interest this side of handicaps.

Showed ability when sixth of 13 on 7f debut at Glorious Goodwood and possibly unsuited by a softer surface when well held over 1m there since. Retains potential now switching to all-weather under Loughnane.
33/1, ran to only a modest level when sixth of 8 in maiden at Salisbury (7f, good to soft) on debut 25 days ago. Will need to step up a good deal on that but improvement is possible.
Supremacy filly who showed plenty to work on amid obvious inexperience when third on Newcastle debut last month but only seventh of 8 on turf at Salisbury since.
Foaled March 23. Saxon Warrior half-sister to 1m winner Maid In Kentucky and 6f-1m winner Ritzy. A newcomer to note in the betting for yard that had a first-time-out 2-y-o winner recently.
Sioux Nation filly who has improved with each start, finishing length second of 9 over C&D 4 weeks ago.

races.name: GavinLynchRacing.com Flat Race
races.verdict: A half-sister to a useful hurdler, DR BONES makes plenty of appeal and she could be up to becoming another winning bumper debutant for her powerful stable. She gets the vote ahead of fellow newcomer Finest Band, while Touch The Clouds is worth another chance to build on his debut promise.

runners.note: €11,000 3-y-o, Order of St George gelding. Half-brother to fairly useful 17f hurdle winner Mr Nicolls and fair chaser Bridle Loanan (2m-19f winner). Off the mark in points at the fifth attempt in May.

€50,000 3-y-o, Bande gelding. Closely related to useful hurdler Pure Genius (19f-3m winner), and half-brother to French hurdler/chaser Desaguadero (2m-2¼m winner). Dam maiden on Flat in France. Possibilities for yard cap
Snow Sky gelding. Brother to fair hurdler Rock On Cowboy (19f winner) and half-brother to fairly useful hurdler Rock House (2m winner), stays 2½m. Worth a market check on debut.
€2,500 3-y-o, Finsceal Fior gelding. Dam ran once over hurdles. Yard not known for winning bumper debutants.

Showed a bit more than on debut when seventh of 14 in bumper at Kilbeggan in June. However, he's failed to repeat that effort in 2 subsequent outings, remote fifth of 11 at the same course last month.
Showed ability when sixth of 24 in bumper at Punchestown in April last year. However, was beaten a long way at the same course next time and absent 15 months since.

Took a step forward when making the frame twice during the summer and soon left behind a lesser effort when runner-up at Tramore last time, beaten only by a useful prospect. Can give another good account.
Shaped well on debut when only narrowly denied in 14-runner bumper at Cork back in July 2024, closing all the way to the line. Has been away from the track for over 2 years since, though.
Berkshire gelding. Dam ran once in bumper. Looks to face a difficult task first time up.

Showed plenty to work on when third of 8 in bumper at Navan (2m) on debut, form working out well. Wasn't in quite the same form when filling the same position in 10-runner event at Naas (19f) in January, but he could yet

€70,000 3-y-o, Maxios gelding. Half-brother to bumper winner Aruntothequeen, stays 2½m, and fairly useful hurdler Atimetodream (2½m winner). First bumper newcomer of the campaign for respected yard. Wears tongue strap.

Was strong in the betting on debut, but shaped as if the run was needed when seventh of 10 in bumper at Kilbeggan 4 months ago. Interesting to see if the support arrives again making first start since leaving R. P. Rath.

Pillar Coral gelding. Half-brother to 4 winners, including fairly useful hurdler/chaser Turbo (17f-2¾m winner) and fair hurdler Roses All The Way (2½m winner). Trainer's most recent bumper runner won on debut back in Oct
Didn't offer much in 2 bumpers during the summer, well held at Roscommon 8 weeks ago. Hood now reached for.

Well-bred mare who showed promise on debut when third of 8 in mares bumper at Sligo (19f) last month. Failed to give her running when tailed off at Kilbeggan 25 days ago, but she's in excellent hands to bounce back. Drop
Soldier of Fortune filly. Half-sister to useful hurdler Printing Dollars (23f winner) and fair hurdler/chaser Lune de La Mer (2½m winner), stays 3m. Noteworthy newcomer for her leading yard.

races.name: Cavani Style & Speed Handicap (Div 1)
races.verdict: Perhaps best to narrow this down to the 3-y-os, with Oisin Murphy's mount RIDGER preferered to Escape Magic. Recent C&D runner-up Mintana may prove best of the older brigade assuming her wide stall isn't too troublesome.

runners.note: Veteran who won at Southwell in April but hasn't seriously threatened since.
C&D winner in March. Also third at Bath in May but below par at Chepstow when last seen in July. Now 1 lb below the mark he defied here but bounce back needed after 74 days off.
Won 7f turf events in her first 2 handicaps. Creditable placed efforts twice since and likely to be bang there if as effective back on all-weather.
Can blow her chance at the start but got her head back in front in Ffos Las classified (1m) event in July. Respectable seventh of 12 in handicap at this course (8.6f) 13 days ago.
Most recent 4 victories have all come at Southwell, the latest over 7f in May. Well held on turf last twice but the return to all-weather may see him in a better light.
NON RUNNER.
Course winner who arrives on the back of a very good second of 9 over C&D 27 days ago. Her draw isn't ideal but still respected.
Completed an all-weather hat-trick in classified company for Ian Williams in January but has struggled since joining current stable.
Not the most consistent and has followed a good second over 6f here in July with 2 poor runs.
Winless since sole victory in December 2024. Below par of late and best watched again.
Remains a maiden after 17 starts. 200/1, last of 9 over C&D last Monday. Easy to look elsewhere.

Improved since tongue tied, finishing second in 6f Ffos Las classified event and close third of 14 in 7f Leicester handicap in recent weeks. Less exposed than most of these and leading claims under Murphy.

races.name: Cavani Style & Speed Handicap (Div 2)
races.verdict: BUNGLE BAY is one of few who obviously arrives in decent form and might be good for a sixth C&D success. Tilsworth Max has saved his best all-weather form to date for Lingfield's polytrack but he will be a threat if close to the form he showed when runner-up there 18 days ago. Sanditon also has a bit of class for this grade if back on his game.

runners.note: C&D winner in January and went in again at Nottingham in June. Has struggled since but the booking of Billy Loughnane takes the eye. Needs checking out in the betting.

Off the mark at Chelmsford in February and doubled his tally in ready fashion over C&D in June. Last couple of runs have been a touch disappointing (including C&D latest) but he is favourably handicapped if back to best.
C&D winner but 19 runs since last win in 2023 and hard to fancy on recent efforts.

Finally off the mark in classified event over this trip at Lingfield in January. Another good run on the polytrack there when close second of 10 this month. Claims if he can reproduce that form back on tapeta.
Five-time C&D winner. 12/1, respectable third of 9 over C&D last Monday. Considered from handy draw.
C&D winner but 14 runs since last win in 2025. 16/1, creditable fourth of 11 in handicap at Bath (1m, good to firm) 16 days ago.
Seems to be going through the motions for present yard, finishing last of 9 at Brighton when last seen in early August. It remains to be seen whether an 8-week break sparks a revival.
Long-standing maiden for Tracy Waggott. A watching brief is advised for new stable (same owner) after 5 months off.
Modest form at best for 3 different stables. Sold out of the Richard Hughes stable for 1,000 gns since finishing last of 11 at Bath 16 days ago.
Long-standing maiden who was last of 10 at Newcastle only 9 days ago. Hard to fancy.
Five-time course winner but he arrives here on a 25-race winless run, including finishing down the field at Ayr when last seen 7 weeks ago.
Ex-Irish maiden who has yet to offer much in a handful of 6f handicaps for new yard in recent weeks. Easy to look elsewhere. Engaged 1.19 Ffos Las Sunday.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Handicap
races.verdict: ZAFAAN does have to prove his stamina for this far on the Flat but arrives on the back of a recent hurdle win and has the services of Billy Loughnane. Trojan Truth makes life awkward for himself with his slow starts but has a bit of class for this grade and is second choice ahead of Wonderful Wendy.

runners.note: Typically slowly away but recorded a turf hat-trick last summer. Placed on 4 occasions this year but never a threat after another very slow start here (1½m) 10 days ago. Blinkers back on. More than capable off this mark
Landed a sixth Southwell in March but has rarely threatened the judge since, including well held back at Southwell on latest start 3 weeks ago.
Improved second on handicap debut at Chepstow (1½m) in June. Hasn't reproduced that level in 2 subsequent outings but she has fewer convictions than most at this level.

Landed a 1¼m Yarmouth classified race in June and arrives on the back of a hurdle win at Worcester (2m) in this headgear combination 24 days ago. Likely to have a big say under Loughnane if stamina holds over the longest
Dual 2m all-weather winner in 2024, including here. Back on track when 3½ lengths third of 9 over 1½m at Chepstow on return in June but not in the same form back there since.

Lightly-raced maiden. Could only manage a well-held seventh of 13 on handicap debut at Windsor (11.5f, good to soft) 30 days ago but has fewer convictions than the rest of these. The cheekpieces she's worn the last twice
Drawn a blank since a Sligo hurdle success in June 2023 but he was second in a 1½m course handicap for Fergal O'Brien in March. Also runner-up on Jersey for new trainer last month.
Sole success came on handicap bow at Lingfield last December. Looked back in form when third switched to classified company at Ayr in June but little impact back in handicaps since.
Returned to form when creditable second of 13 in handicap at Windsor (11.5f) last month but not in the same form when sixth at Epsom since. Steps up in trip now tackling tapeta for the first time.
Half-brother to a useful sort  but has yet to show much, including on Pontefract handicap debut just 4 days ago. First-time cheekpieces need to spark improvement.

races.name: Free Race Replays On attheraces.com Handicap
races.verdict: CROWN THE FUTURE has already won here and looks the most solid option after his good second over C&D last time. Ernie McCrew was a place behind the selection on that occasion and has won at Lingfield since. Wild Rosie and Oisin Murphy's mount Roserunner also make the shortlist.

runners.note: Understandably looked rusty back from 11 months off when sixth of 8 in maiden at Lingfield (1m, all-weather) 18 days ago. Entitled to come on for the run and brings unexposed potential to this handicap debut.

Won a 1m Lingfield maiden second time up in December. Close second on C&D handicap debut in January and back on form when third of 10 at Windsor (1m) when last seen in June. Oisin Murphy gets the leg up back from a break
Creditable fourth of 8 in a handicap at Lingfield (7f) last month but failed to build on it when only ninth of 14 at Kempton (1m) since.
Long-standing maiden who was well held in 1m Kempton handicap a fortnight ago. A first-time tongue tie needs to have a positive effect.

Got off the mark in 7f handicap at Lingfield (all-weather) in August and backed it up with a good second at Windsor (6f) a week later. Not so good back at Windsor in first-time cheekpieces (retained) last time and now st
Probably flattered on her sole 2-y-o start given her struggles this year. Wears first-time cheekpieces.
Well held in 3 qualifying runs at up to 1m over the summer. Handicaps provide him with a more realistic chance but would need to see market support to consider.

Gained reward for some good placed efforts in recent months (including C&D) when getting off the mark in 1m Lingfield handicap in first-time cheekpieces (retained) 16 days ago. Respected off 4 lb higher.
Course winner. 10/1, good second (Ernie McCrew third) of 12 over C&D 21 days ago, clear of rest. Major player under Marquand.

Ran one of this season's better races when fourth of 10 in handicap at Lingfield (1¼m, all-weather) 18 days ago. Has a hood and cheekpieces combined for the first time here. Claims if able to back up that Lingfield run.
Lightly-raced sort who was caught too far back and met trouble when eighth of 12 on C&D handicap debut 21 days ago and can be given another chance to show what she can do from this mark.
Lightly-raced maiden. Good third of 8 on handicap debut at Southwell (1m) last month and had an excuse (denied a clear run) when down the field over this C&D since.
Has finished well held on all 5 turf starts, including a couple of low-grade handicaps.

races.name: Cavani Winning Form Handicap
races.verdict: A tight handicap. Given it was only his second outing of the year BONA FORTUNA might be able to build on his last Brighton second. Too Darn Good won in taking fashion over C&D 3 weeks ago and is feared most ahead of Nogo's Dream, who is quirky but is down to his lowest mark for a long time.

runners.note: Dual winner in 2024. Runner-up 4 times since, including at Brighton (5.3f, good) 27 days ago. That was only his second outing of the season so he's fresh for the time of year. Makes all-weather debut.
Winner of back-to-back all-weather nurseries at the end of last year (including C&D). More miss than hit this season but is feasibly handicapped if a return to all-weather sparks a revival.
C&D winner. Added to his tally at Yarmouth (5f) in May but the handicapper has been winning the argument since and he remains 3 lb above that last win mark. First-time blinkers and tongue tie go on.

Back to form under an attacking ride when getting off the mark in an 11-runner event at Windsor in July. Went off too hard there next time but settled better with cheekpieces removed and produced a career best to see off
Doubled her tally at Yarmouth (5f, firm) in July. Creditable third of 9 in handicap at Sandown (5f, soft) 17 days ago.
Quirky sort but often makes the frame and 2 of his 4 wins have been gained under Oisin Murphy. Back on a good mark.
Front runner who recorded a first handicap success at Brighton (5.3f, good) 27 days ago. Likely to remain competitive off 5 lb higher.

Successful on all-weather over 5f at Newcastle and Lingfield in the spring. Ended his time with Richard Spencer with thirds over C&D and at Windsor in the first half of this month. New connections recently acquired him f

races.name: Free Digital Racecard At raceday-ready.com Handicap
races.verdict: THE ANTHONY GOVER escapes a penalty for last week's win and is taken to overcome the outside stall and land a C&D hat-trick. Pipily is another with good recent C&D form and is second choice ahead of Vega Storm and Variety Act.

runners.note: Improved form when third of 7 in 7f Catterick maiden last August but well held in Newmarket handicap on final start and suffered a similar fate on 1m Newbury reappearance in July. Steps up in trip back from 10 weeks off.
Has shown the odd quirk but he won a pair of 1m turf handicaps in July. Two lesser runs have followed, though.

Showed promise in 2 of his 3 qualifying runs in the winter and might have needed the run after 6 months off when fourth of 6 on C&D handicap debut 27 days ago. Has cheekpieces added now. Remains unexposed.
Got off the mark at Ripon (1m) in June. Not discredited on next 2 outings and possibly simply failed to cope with heavy ground at Haydock last time.
Good pedigree but hasn't shown much sign that she can live up to it so far, including well held on Beverley handicap debut (1¼m, heavy) 30 days ago.
On a hat-trick after a pair of C&D wins this month, the first one gained under Billy Loughnane. The second came in an apprentice race last week and he makes obvious appeal turned out unpenalised.

Made all to get off the mark at the fourth attempt in a 1¼m Lingfield maiden in testing conditions in June but has finished well held in 4 handicaps since. First-time cheekpieces need to have a positive effect.

Showed improved form upped to 1¼m when just denied by a subsequent winner at Newmarket in July. Built on that effort at the second time of asking when ½-length third of 10 over this C&D 27 days ago. Player under Marquand
Has reached the frame 3 times in handicaps at up to 1m and the way he plugged on for fourth at Southwell last time suggests this slightly longer trip is worth a go.
Well-connected gelding who showed more than previously when fifth of 13 on handicap debut at Southwell (1m) 63 days ago. May do better.
Gained a first success when making all in handicap at Leicester in June but below-form seventh on all 3 starts since, including to The Anthony Gover over C&D 21 days ago.
Well held all 4 starts, including 1½m Kempton handicap debut 33 days ago. Back down in trip.
